title: Fixing Distraction Is a Test of Company Culture
coreMove: Diagnose workplace distraction by looking at the norms people are rewarded or punished for following.
sourcePressure: The chapter moves to workplace culture, shifting blame from individual weakness to norms, coordination, and permission systems.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would tell employees to focus harder inside a culture that punishes focus.

hook: Fixing Distraction Is a Test of Company Culture as a labeled topic opener
counterintuition: phones are not the problem by itself
tryThisNow: set a timer and notice your distractions
examples: reused old-package object-anchor shell from earlier Indistractable run

exampleSpecs.domain: regional ambulance billing office with instant-response expectations
exampleSpecs.audience: billing supervisor watching staff apologize for every delayed reply
exampleSpecs.stakes: claims errors rise when speed is rewarded over accuracy
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she maps which praise and scolding make immediate chat replies feel mandatory
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A denied-claim packet sits beside a response-time praise note.

exampleSpecs.domain: architecture firm celebrating late-night render messages
exampleSpecs.audience: associate who notices all praise goes to visible exhaustion
exampleSpecs.stakes: design quality suffers when attention theater becomes status
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he points to the project chat where midnight replies get applause and daytime focus gets suspicion
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A render log glows beside a midnight applause thread.

exampleSpecs.domain: warehouse safety team after repeated scanner pings
exampleSpecs.audience: safety lead tracing why pickers answer alerts while driving carts
exampleSpecs.stakes: injury risk is cultural when the system rewards instant compliance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she follows the incentive trail from scanner metrics to cart behavior before blaming workers
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A scanner metrics printout lies beside a cart-route badge.

exampleSpecs.domain: remote software support team with always-open video rooms
exampleSpecs.audience: team lead whose people fear stepping out of video
exampleSpecs.stakes: presence pressure replaces actual support quality
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks what happens to someone who turns camera off to solve a hard ticket
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A support ticket board sits beside an always-open room tile.

exampleSpecs.domain: hotel housekeeping department with conflicting priorities
exampleSpecs.audience: manager who tells staff quality matters while rewarding fastest room turnover
exampleSpecs.stakes: attention cannot stabilize under contradictory signals
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, errors are called personal; after, the manager identifies the speed bonus as the trigger
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A room-inspection card rests beside a turnover bonus chart.

exampleSpecs.domain: university advising office during enrollment week
exampleSpecs.audience: director whose advisors are told to be careful and instantly available
exampleSpecs.stakes: students receive worse guidance when culture demands both
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes the two conflicting expectations on the intake board and chooses which one the office will protect
exampleSpecs.firstImage: An enrollment intake board stands beside a careful-review pledge.
